title: Transfer E*TRADE Stocks and RSUs to Another Broker
summary: Move E*TRADE stocks or vested RSU shares to a broker that supports Indian residents without selling, or sell and wire the proceeds. Steps, fees and Indian tax.
body_markdown:
You can move your E*TRADE holdings to another broker without selling them. E*TRADE supports outgoing transfers through ACATS, and if you would rather exit, you can sell and wire the cash instead.


This guide is for Indian residents in two situations. Either you opened an E*TRADE brokerage account while living in the US and have since returned, or your employer's RSU or ESPP shares are delivered through a stock plan account on etrade.com.


In both cases the account does little for you as an Indian resident. It gives you no Indian tax reports and no way to keep investing from India. For the general rules on moving RSU shares, see[Can I transfer my RSUs to another broker?](https://paasa.com/blog/can-i-transfer-my-rsus-to-another-broker)


## Table of contents


- How can I move my E*TRADE holdings without selling?
- How the transfer works
- What can and cannot transfer from E*TRADE
- What does it cost and how long does it take?
- If your RSUs are in a stock plan account on E*TRADE
- Moving cash from E*TRADE
- Tax and reporting after the move
- Transferring your E*TRADE holdings to Paasa
- About Paasa


## How can I move my E*TRADE holdings without selling?


E*TRADE supports outgoing transfers through ACATS (Automated Customer Account Transfer Service), the standard US system for moving brokerage assets between firms. Your shares move from E*TRADE to the new broker as they are, without being sold.


Selling everything in order to switch is not necessary. A sale creates a capital gain in India on every position that has risen in value, while an[in-kind transfer](https://paasa.com/blog/can-you-transfer-us-stocks-to-another-broker-without-selling) does not.


A regular E*TRADE brokerage account is meant for US residents. Some returning NRIs keep access for a while and others find the account restricted sooner, so it is easier to transfer while the account is in good standing than after restrictions have been applied.


## How the transfer works


The transfer is started by your new broker, not by E*TRADE. The standard process looks like this:


- You open an account at the new broker.
- You give the new broker your E*TRADE account details, statements and identification documents.
- The new broker submits the request through ACATS, which notifies E*TRADE.
- E*TRADE validates the request within 1 business day and delivers the assets within 3 business days.
- Your shares appear in the new account.


You do not need to call E*TRADE or tell them in advance. Under[FINRA's customer account transfer rules](https://www.finra.org/rules-guidance/key-topics/customer-account-transfers) , the firm you are leaving has to act on a valid transfer request.


## What can and cannot transfer from E*TRADE


These assets transfer in-kind:


- Whole shares of US-listed stocks
- Whole shares of US-listed ETFs
- US Treasuries and bonds
- Settled cash


These do not transfer in-kind:


- Fractional shares, which are sold automatically, with the cash following separately
- E*TRADE-branded and Morgan Stanley proprietary mutual funds that the new broker does not carry
- Unsettled trades
- Margin positions
- Options contracts


If you hold proprietary mutual funds, the rest of your portfolio can still move in-kind. Those funds are sold before or during the transfer and the proceeds move as cash, which creates a taxable event on those positions only.


## What does it cost and how long does it take?


E*TRADE's[pricing page](https://us.etrade.com/what-we-offer/pricing-and-rates) lists USD 75 for a full outgoing account transfer and USD 25 for a partial one, and the partial fee is waived if more than USD 5,000 remains in the account afterwards.


E*TRADE validates the request within 1 business day and delivers within 3 business days, so an ACATS transfer typically completes in 3 to 5 business days. Dividends declared before the transfer date are received at E*TRADE first and then swept to the new account as a residual transfer, typically within 30 days of the main transfer settling.


## If your RSUs are in a stock plan account on E*TRADE


Employer equity is handled by Morgan Stanley at Work, which owns E*TRADE. Morgan Stanley describes the current stock plan account as the one previously known as Shareworks, StockPlan Connect or the E*TRADE stock plan account. It is separate from an E*TRADE brokerage account, even when you reach both with one login.


That difference decides your route:


- **Shares in an E*TRADE brokerage account.** According to Morgan Stanley's[stock plan FAQ](https://www.morganstanley.com/atwork/employees/stockplan-faq-sw) , participants who open or link an E*TRADE brokerage account have their vested, unrestricted shares moved into it automatically. That linked account is generally available to US residents. Shares held there are in a regular brokerage account, so they follow the ACATS process above.
- **Shares still in the stock plan account.** Participants outside the US usually sell and transact from the stock plan account itself. Morgan Stanley's[guide for participants outside the US](https://www.morganstanley.com/cs/pdf/et_account_management_etrade_com_non_us_english.pdf) covers selling and receiving proceeds from the At Work section of etrade.com.


Shares still in the stock plan account can also move without being sold, but usually through Morgan Stanley's own share transfer process rather than ACATS, which can take longer. Tell the Paasa team which platform you are on before you begin, so that they can take you through the right steps. Only vested shares can move, and your company's trading windows and holding rules continue to apply until the shares have left the plan.


## Moving cash from E*TRADE


The other route is to sell and move the US dollars. In the At Work section of etrade.com, the "Selling or Exercising Options" tab takes you through the sale. Once it settles, Morgan Stanley's guide says the proceeds can be sent by check, by wire, or to an eligible E*TRADE or Morgan Stanley account.


Wire details are saved under At Work, then My Account, then Add/Edit Wire Instruction. Morgan Stanley's[wire instructions guide](https://www.morganstanley.com/cs/pdf/et_wire_disbursement_guide.pdf) notes two things that matter here:


- Participants outside the US can send wires only to an account in their own name, and the name on the receiving account has to match the name on the stock plan account.
- The currency defaults to the local currency of the destination bank. To keep the money in dollars, select USD from the Select Currency dropdown when you choose the wire for your proceeds.


To send the proceeds to Paasa, the steps in the app are:


- **Step 1:** Download the Paasa app and complete your KYC to open your account, if you have not already.
- **Step 2:** Open the app and tap "Transfer investments".
- **Step 3:** Select E*TRADE as your broker.
- **Step 4:** Select "Transfer cash".
- **Step 5:** Follow the on-screen instructions, and use the account details Paasa provides when you set up the wire.


Selling is a taxable event, unlike a transfer of shares. Once the cash is sitting abroad, the[FEMA 180-day rule](https://paasa.com/blog/fema-180-day-rule) applies, so the proceeds have to be reinvested or brought back to India within 180 days.


## Tax and reporting after the move


A transfer of shares between two accounts that both belong to you is not a sale. You own the same shares before and after, so there is no capital gain and nothing to pay in India because of the move.


Your cost and holding period carry over. For RSU shares, the cost is the rupee value that was taxed as salary when the shares vested, and the holding period runs from the vesting date. The transfer changes neither.[Capital gains tax on RSU shares](https://paasa.com/blog/capital-gains-tax-rsu-shares) explains how the gain is worked out when you do sell.


Download your statements and cost basis records from E*TRADE before you start, because you will need the original dates and US dollar values for your Indian return.


Schedule FA still applies. If you are resident and ordinarily resident, you report the shares and the foreign account they are held in for every calendar year in which you held them. In the year of the move, both the old and the new account are reported. See[Schedule FA for RSU holders](https://paasa.com/blog/schedule-fa-rsu-holders) for the tables and values.


The transfer does not use your LRS limit, since the shares are already abroad and no money leaves India.


## Transferring your E*TRADE holdings to Paasa


Your Paasa account is held in your own name with Interactive Brokers as custodian, and E*TRADE holdings can be transferred to it directly through ACATS. Step-by-step instructions for E*TRADE are in the Paasa app. Complete your sign-up, open the transfer guide for E*TRADE and follow it to start the transfer.


The Paasa team can help with the transfer, including working out which of your funds will move in-kind and which will need to be sold first. If you would like someone to walk you through your E*TRADE dashboard, write to support@paasa.com or message your relationship manager in the app.


## About Paasa


[Paasa](https://paasa.com/rsu) is a global investing platform built for Indian and Asian investors, giving you direct access to stocks and ETFs across the US, UK, Europe and Asia from one account.


- **Guided transfers:** Paasa guides you through the transfer for your specific broker, whether you move the shares or sell and send the US dollars.
- **Diversify once the shares arrive:** Invest in markets across 11 countries, including European-domiciled UCITS ETFs that are estate-tax safe for Indian residents.
- **Tax reports built for your ITR:** Year-end reports aligned with Indian ITR requirements, including Schedule CG and Schedule FA, are sent automatically and can be shared with your CA.
